markdown_report:
Select a **catalog-competition audit for the corrected GRU4Rec**. At 0% progress, this is a feasible diagnostic before another training intervention. A sampled/full-catalog gap is mathematically expected; its size alone establishes neither an implementation bug nor a model weakness. No validation improvement is established.

Three starting insights guide this choice. First, positive training margins measure sampled discrimination, so further margin growth need not improve HR@10. Second, latest-item deletion causes larger rank changes than oldest-item deletion, demonstrating temporal reliance without establishing that stronger recency helps. Third, module checks pass while generated-predictor parity remains unverified; serialization checks cannot resolve writer or routing correctness.

Three literature insights sharpen the direction. Hidasi and Czapp [1] and Krichene and Rendle [6] demonstrate sampled-ranking distortions, including model-order reversals. Pereira et al. [2] distinguish reliability dimensions; repeated sampling reduces sampling noise without recovering the full-catalog objective automatically. Prakash et al. [3] motivate training-frequency strata, without establishing disparities in these checkpoints.

The framework separates three research directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competition | Sampled margins | Exact eligible-catalog ranks and analytic sampled-hit probabilities | Training fit versus generalization |
| Memory | History perturbations | Lag-dependent state/score sensitivity | Useful versus merely retained information |
| Optimization | Aggregate losses | Position-group gradient comparisons | Local opposition versus harmful interference |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores denote originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more engineering.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog-competition audit [1–3,6] | 2/6/4 | Directly describes omitted competition using established mathematics | Diagnostic integration has limited novelty; isolated sampling and exact scoring require care |
| Lag-dependent GRU sensitivity [4] | 4/6/6 | Separates state retention from target discrimination | Attribution depends on perturbations and careful recurrent differentiation |
| Position-group gradient audit [5] | 4/6/5 | Locates opposing updates within one network using standard autograd | Local conflict need not harm generalization; parameter-group comparisons add overhead |

For the selected audit, freeze each category model and reuse one isolated cache of at most 256 training prefixes across all probes. Exclude original-history items from competitors, retain the target once, and score the eligible training catalog in deterministic chunks. Report exact rank, target-minus-tenth-competitor margin, sampled-hit probability, and expected sampled-hit/full-miss frequency. Stratify by training popularity and history length, retaining support and undefined cases.

With C competitors, M preceding the target and n=min(99,C), the sampled hit probability is P[Hypergeometric(C,M,n)≤9]. This transforms training ranks into expected sampled outcomes; it supplies no independent generalization evidence. Crossing rank distributions can reverse aggregate model comparisons; pointwise dominance cannot under identical sampling conditions. No additional models are trained or loaded for this audit.

Keep results descriptive and selection exclusively on pinned macro validation HR@10. Anonymous prefixes receive no user-bootstrap intervals. Preserve diagnostic APIs, left-padding alignment, fresh recurrent states, four-category routing, and one checkpoint per category. Verify the generated predictor when callable; otherwise retain the parity limitation. All diagnostic GPU time consumes the shared budget.

idea.description: Add a bounded, training-only catalog-competition audit to the existing GRU4Rec diagnostic adapter. For each cached prefix, score the eligible catalog using its single trained category model, measure exact target rank and omitted competition, and calculate the target's hit probability under uniform sampling of up to 99 unique negatives. Interpret these quantities as training-fit diagnostics under an explicitly declared candidate population, without treating an expected sampled/full-catalog gap as evidence of a defect.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish training separation and temporal reliance, but neither establishes catalog-wide generalization or validation improvement. Exact competition measurements describe where targets lie beyond a small sampled candidate set and can expose masking or scoring inconsistencies. They do not independently distinguish memorization, popularity shortcuts or useful personalization. At 0% progress, this bounded audit remains preferable to more expensive recurrent attribution or gradient-conflict probes; regularization, sampling or loss interventions should follow only as separate controlled hypotheses accepted through the unchanged host validation metric.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions, preserving existing probes and every ModelView interface. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Keep the public loader yield (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors.

Build one bounded diagnostic cache and reuse it for all probes, rather than iterating the supplied training loader separately for existing and new measurements. Cache at most ten batches and 256 prefixes per category in deterministic sampler order. Use the family-specific sample_batch implementation and identical training-only sampling semantics through an independently constructed loader with dedicated generators and num_workers=0. Do not advance the active training iterator, its sampler, worker processes or prefetch queues. Establish this separate-loader or prebuilt-cache interface explicitly during integration; the supplied public batch tuple alone does not provide a reproducible loader factory or user identity. If neither isolated access mechanism is available, report the new audit as unavailable with its reason rather than consuming the live training iterator or claiming RNG isolation.

Use diagnostic seed 42 and preserve affected Python random, NumPy, CPU Torch, selected CUDA and explicit generator states in finally. torch.random.fork_rng covers CPU and specified CUDA states, but does not restore Python, NumPy, explicit generators or DataLoader workers. Dedicated diagnostic generators should never share state with training. Record seeds, software versions, device, precision, chunk size, cache sampling order and supplied user/prefix identifiers where available. Anonymous rows remain prefixes, not identified distinct users. Save bounded results and the protocol beneath the current trial directory. Do not read other trials or their checkpoints.

Use only training histories and aligned training targets; do not inspect validation or test files for this audit. Training targets contributed to fitting, so exact ranks measure training fit, including possible memorization. Prefix sampling can overweight users with repeated rows or longer histories. Report duplicate-prefix counts and actual support without silently deduplicating or claiming population representativeness. Report explicit absence of stable user identifiers and omit user-bootstrap intervals. If identifiers become available, aggregate prefixes within users before user-level summaries; any resulting uncertainty remains conditional on the fitted model and diagnostic sampling design.

Run the actual module in eval mode and torch.inference_mode(), restoring its prior mode in finally. Compute features once for each cached history batch and reuse them across candidate chunks. Every independent history starts from fresh recurrent state. Gather the feature at the maximum nonzero sequence index, never nonpadding count minus one in the original left-padded layout. Skip empty histories and zero aligned targets with explicit counts. Confirm causal sequence/target alignment. Preserve existing correctness checks and checkpoint roundtrip checks.

Keep the corrected baseline's padding semantics when they pass. If packed GRU execution is needed, first compact nonpadding items chronologically into right-padded rows, pass CPU lengths with enforce_sorted=False, exclude empty rows from packing, and restore per-position outputs to original left-padded locations. Directly packing left-padded rows is incorrect. Any repair changing training semantics requires retraining and matching changes in the predictor writer; this diagnostic proposal does not assume such a repair is needed.

Define the catalog as sorted unique real item IDs occurring in user_train['History'], excluding reserved tokens and checking embedding bounds. Record catalog construction and size. For each prefix, define competitors by excluding the target and original observed prefix from that catalog. Include the target exactly once even if repeated in its prefix. A target absent from the declared training catalog is a protocol error to report explicitly, not an invitation to extend the catalog using held-out information. This population intentionally includes other known training interactions outside the prefix; they are ranking competitors rather than verified dislikes. It differs from full-user-positive exclusion used by some training samplers and is not claimed to reproduce host eligibility or simulator unseen-item filtering. Freeze this population for every metric and redraw concerning that prefix.

Score catalog items in ascending item-ID chunks through predict_score(features, items), using the existing scoring contract without changing model scores. Predeclare a conservative initial chunk size, for example 4096 items, and record any memory-driven reduction. Avoid a full prefix-by-catalog score matrix. Count competitors preceding the target using descending score and ascending item-ID ties. Maintain the ten highest-ranked competitors using an exact lexicographic merge; torch.topk alone does not guarantee item-ID tie ordering. Compute the target score through the same scoring path and precision. Do not introduce a numerical tie tolerance silently. Record exact target ties and top-10 boundary ties where defined. Chunk-size parity on a small deterministic cache checks numerical sensitivity; fixed seeds do not guarantee identical results across platforms or releases.

For each valid prefix report eligible competitor count C, preceding competitor count M, exact target rank 1+M, full diagnostic hit indicator 1[M<=9], and target score minus the tenth-highest competitor score. The latter is null with a reason when C<10. Under exact ties its sign alone does not determine rank because item IDs break ties. If target or competitor scores are nonfinite, invalidate the prefix's ranking metrics and report counts and reasons; do not drop individual competitors and thereby change eligibility. With finite scores and C=0, rank is one and both diagnostic hit quantities equal one.

For n=min(99,C) negatives drawn uniformly without replacement, X~Hypergeometric(C,M,n), and sampled diagnostic hit probability is P(X<=9). Use scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(min(9,n), C, M, n) when C>0 and handle C=0 explicitly. Record actual candidate count 1+n. Report category means of full diagnostic hit indicators and analytic sampled-hit probabilities. Expected sampled-hit/full-miss frequency is the mean of P(X<=9)*1[M>=10]; the difference between expected sampled and full hit rates equals this frequency under the declared identical eligibility and ranking rules. Report complete rank summaries or an empirical rank distribution rather than only this gap. These quantities are not host validation HR@10.

A small fixed diagnostic redraw set may cross-check sampling implementation but is unnecessary for estimating an analytically available probability. If used, predeclare 32 redraws per prefix using a dedicated RNG, sampling unique eligible IDs, and compare observed hit counts with the analytic probabilities while acknowledging Monte Carlo noise. Repeated draws reduce conditional sampling noise; they do not make sampled HR@10 an estimator of full-catalog HR@10 or add independent users. No redraw results or parity success are claimed here.

Define target popularity by training interaction counts. Sort catalog items by descending count then ascending item ID, and split item ranks into three bands with boundaries ceil(V/3) and ceil(2V/3), recording item counts and interaction mass per band. Use history-length bins 1, 2–5, 6–20 and 21+, and report repeat-target status and candidate-count strata. Report support, descriptive prefix means, exact-rank distributions and analytic expected sampled hits within each category and stratum. Keep sparse cells visible without strong interpretations. Head/middle/tail here means item-rank thirds, not interaction-mass thirds. Optional competitor-popularity counts must use these same frozen training-derived bands.

The expected sampled/full gap is an ordinary consequence of sampling and cannot diagnose a particular model weakness by itself. Under identical candidate populations and tie rules, pointwise rank dominance cannot reverse expected sampled-hit ordering; crossing rank distributions can produce aggregate reversals. This observation motivates distributional reporting, not loading or training comparison models within the audit. Any later comparison uses independently authorized single-model trials and available reported results, without reading other-trial artifacts, reusing checkpoints or combining predictions.

Do not optimize these diagnostic strata or simulator feedback as selection metrics. Full-catalog training fit may reward memorization, and training-derived popularity strata reveal associations rather than causal shortcut mechanisms. Strong rank performance does not establish compatibility, ownership needs, current intent, mood or diversity. Only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are available. Do not use unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores or simulator traits. Category breakdown lists remain empty with an availability explanation. Undefined metrics return null with reasons rather than zeros.

Keep the corrected GRU4Rec architecture, objective, optimizer and inference unchanged for this diagnostic proposal. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, 200 batches per epoch, maximum 200 epochs, single-GPU execution, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], fixed splits and the pinned evaluator. Retain exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint per category, without fusion, independently fitted auxiliary scores, averaging or checkpoint reuse. Keep twenty training users, five/category, receiving full-catalog unseen-item recommendations through the native simulator; this separate diagnostic audit does not redefine that population. Accept subsequent changes only through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Repeated validation-based selection can still overfit.

Charge caching, diagnostic scoring, runtime probes, debugging and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Record elapsed diagnostic GPU time and peak memory. Stop the audit at a predeclared remaining-budget guard between complete prefix batches and report completed support and truncation. Do not assume catalog scoring is affordable before measuring it or sacrifice completion of the required four-category training/evaluation trial to an optional diagnostic expansion.

Verify actual generated working/predict.py scores and category routing against selected checkpoints when an executable predictor interface is available, including empty and single-item histories and different left-padding widths. Start FP32 comparisons at rtol=1e-5 and atol=1e-6 and record observed differences. Module serialization parity alone does not verify the predictor writer. Keep architecture and predictor writer synchronized if any later change is made. No execution, parity success, runtime affordability or validation gain is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        prior_mode = self.view.model.training
        try:
            # Integration requirement: independent family-specific loader/cache.
            # Never advance the active training iterator.
            with preserve_python_numpy_torch_cuda_and_explicit_rng_states():
                cache = isolated_diagnostic_cache(
                    train_loader,
                    family_sample_batch=family_specific_sample_batch,
                    dedicated_seed=42,
                    num_workers=0,
                    max_batches=10,
                    max_prefixes=256,
                )
                if cache is unavailable:
                    return existing_results_or_unavailable_with_reasons()

                self.view.model.eval()
                with torch.inference_mode():
                    # All probes reuse this cache; no second loader traversal.
                    results = retain_existing_measured_probes(cache)
                    catalog, counts = sorted_training_catalog_and_counts(
                        self.view.user_train['History'], reserved_ids)
                    bands = item_rank_thirds(counts, tie_break='ascending_item_id')

                    for batch in cache:
                        if predeclared_budget_guard_reached():
                            record_truncation_and_completed_support()
                            break
                        features = self.view.log2feats(batch.sequence)
                        # Actual GRU starts from fresh zero state for every row.
                        for b in range(len(batch.sequence)):
                            sequence = batch.sequence[b]
                            positions = torch.where(sequence.ne(0))[0]
                            if positions.numel() == 0:
                                record_skip('empty_history')
                                continue
                            t = int(positions.max())
                            target = int(batch.positive[b, t])
                            if target == 0:
                                record_skip('missing_target')
                                continue
                            if target not in catalog:
                                record_protocol_error('target_outside_training_catalog')
                                continue

                            final = features[b, t]
                            target_score = score_one_via_predict_score(final, target)
                            excluded = set(sequence[positions].tolist())
                            excluded |= reserved_ids | {target}
                            eligible = sorted_catalog_without(catalog, excluded)
                            C, M = 0, 0
                            top_competitors = exact_lexicographic_topk(10)
                            finite = isfinite(target_score)
                            ties = 0
                            for items in chunks(eligible, size=4096):
                                scores = self.view.predict_score(final, items)
                                if not all_finite(scores):
                                    finite = False
                                    break
                                tied = scores.eq(target_score)
                                precedes = scores.gt(target_score) | (
                                    tied & items.lt(target))
                                C += len(items)
                                M += int(precedes.sum())
                                ties += int(tied.sum())
                                top_competitors.merge(
                                    scores, items,
                                    order=('descending_score', 'ascending_item_id'))

                            if not finite:
                                record_undefined_prefix('nonfinite_score')
                                continue
                            n = min(99, C)
                            p_hit = (1.0 if C == 0 else float(
                                hypergeom.cdf(min(9, n), C, M, n)))
                            full_hit = int(M <= 9)
                            margin = (target_score - top_competitors.score_at(10)
                                      if C >= 10 else None)
                            record(
                                rank=1 + M,
                                competitors=C,
                                preceding=M,
                                target_score_ties=ties,
                                full_diagnostic_hit=full_hit,
                                diagnostic_candidate_count=1 + n,
                                expected_sampled_diagnostic_hit=p_hit,
                                expected_sampled_hit_full_miss=p_hit * (1-full_hit),
                                target_minus_tenth_competitor=margin,
                                margin_undefined_reason=(
                                    'fewer_than_ten_competitors' if C < 10 else None),
                                training_popularity_band=bands[target],
                                history_length=len(positions),
                                repeat_target=target in sequence[positions].tolist(),
                                user_id=provided_id_or_none(batch, b),
                            )
                    return {
                        'metrics': aggregate_with_support_and_rank_distributions(results),
                        'metric_definitions': explicit_protocol_and_limits(),
                    }
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(prior_mode)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return grounded_prompt(
        raw_diagnosis['metrics'], raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        distinguish_training_fit_from_generalization=True,
        distinguish_diagnostics_from_host_validation=True,
        explain_expected_sampling_gap_without_calling_it_a_defect=True,
        require_support_and_undefined_reasons=True,
        forbid_unsupported_causal_or_preference_claims=True,
    )

# Helper functions denote required host integration, not supplied executable APIs.
# Preserve existing probes if isolated caching is unavailable; report limitations.
# Never train/load additional predictors, fuse scores, or change host selection.

originality.positive: Integrates exact eligible-catalog competition, analytic sampled-hit probabilities, training-popularity strata and isolated diagnostic caching within the GRU4Rec compatibility contract.
originality.negative: Exact ranks, hypergeometric analysis, popularity breakdowns and RNG isolation are established techniques; this is a careful diagnostic adaptation rather than a new algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Can reveal candidate-mask inconsistencies and characterize training-rank distributions, providing concrete hypotheses for subsequent controlled loss, sampling or regularization experiments.
future_potential.negative: The analytic sampling gap is expected, and training-prefix measurements remain vulnerable to memorization. Their value for predicting improvements in pinned validation HR@10 is unestablished.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing scoring hooks and standard distribution calculations without changing architecture, checkpoint format or inference scores.
code_difficulty.negative: An isolated family-specific cache, exact tie handling, deterministic bounded scoring, budget accounting and actual generated-predictor parity require more integration than the scoring formula alone suggests.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp (2023): evaluation flaws in recommender systems
contributions: Demonstrates distortions introduced by sampled evaluation in GRU4Rec experiments.
Relates sampled-hit probabilities to full rank through a hypergeometric distribution.
Motivates reporting exact rank distributions alongside sampled outcomes.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed training-prefix audit predicts improvement on this benchmark.
Analytic probabilities require matching eligibility, uniform sampling without replacement and ranking rules.
An expected sampled/full-catalog gap alone does not establish a bug or a particular model weakness.

related_work.title: Pereira et al. (2025): reliability of sampling-based recommendation evaluation
contributions: Examines sampling reliability through fidelity, resolution, robustness and recovery of model rankings.
Motivates separating sampling variability from the objective measured by an evaluation protocol.
limitations: Does not supply results for the four category models considered here.
Sampling reliability analysis does not itself improve a recommender.
Repeated diagnostic draws do not resolve training-prefix memorization or create independent users.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): popularity disparities in sequential recommendation
contributions: Reports head, middle and tail disparities obscured by aggregate sequential-recommendation metrics.
Investigates popularity effects associated with random training negatives.
limitations: Reported disparities cannot be assumed to hold for the supplied GRU4Rec checkpoints.
Popularity strata describe behavior without identifying user preferences or causal mechanisms.
Band definitions must be stated explicitly because item-rank thirds differ from interaction-mass thirds.

related_work.title: Gating creates slow modes and controls phase-space complexity in GRUs and LSTMs
contributions: Connects recurrent gating to memory timescales and dynamical behavior.
Motivates separating hidden-state retention from downstream score sensitivity.
limitations: Gate behavior alone does not establish useful memory or recommendation accuracy.
Does not validate the proposed GRU4Rec sensitivity audit.
Stronger recency or longer retention is not established as desirable for this benchmark.

related_work.title: Gradient-conflict research referenced in the supplied search results (2024)
contributions: Motivates examining competing updates within shared model parameters.
limitations: The proposed sequence-position adaptation remains unvalidated.
Negative gradient cosine is local opposition and does not establish harmful generalization.
The supplied search summary does not establish a direct GRU4Rec contribution; bibliographic details and applicability require verification before stronger attribution.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle (2020): On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes inconsistency between sampled and full-ranking recommendation metrics.
Shows that model-comparison reversals can persist in expectation, rather than arising only from sampling noise.
Supports distinguishing repeated-sampling precision from recovery of the full-catalog objective.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the pinned host selection metric.
Does not establish any ranking reversal for the supplied category models.
Pointwise dominance cannot reverse under identical sampling and tie conditions; aggregate reversals require differing rank distributions.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: DataLoader and data-loading randomness
contributions: Documents DataLoader generators, worker processes and worker randomness.
Supports using a separate diagnostic loader with dedicated generators and num_workers=0.
limitations: Restoring parent RNG states does not rewind worker processes, prefetch queues or an advanced training iterator.
The host's family-specific sampler must expose an isolated construction or cache mechanism.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: random number generation
contributions: Documents Torch RNG state management and fork_rng for CPU and selected devices.
limitations: Torch RNG isolation does not automatically preserve Python, NumPy or explicit sampler-generator states.
RNG restoration does not reverse data-loader consumption.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: pack_padded_sequence
contributions: Documents sequence packing, CPU lengths and enforce_sorted handling.
Supports compacting valid histories into chronological prefixes before packed GRU execution.
limitations: Direct packing of left-padded histories does not preserve the intended valid sequence.
Per-position outputs must be restored to the original layout to preserve target alignment.
Empty histories need explicit handling outside packed execution.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: torch.topk
contributions: Warns that indices of tied elements are not guaranteed to be stable.
Motivates an explicit lexicographic score/item-ID rule when merging candidate chunks.
limitations: Calling topk alone does not implement the declared deterministic item-ID tie ordering.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: reproducibility
contributions: Documents reproducibility controls and limitations across platforms, devices and releases.
limitations: Fixed seeds alone do not guarantee identical numerical results across environments.
The audit must record its environment and observed parity differences rather than claim universal bitwise reproducibility.
